notes: The first part says that the cycle Z gives a map from R^1 g_* to R^(2n−1) f_*, then a map on H^1(S,−). The compatibility identifies u(x) with the image of u(x′). It concludes that vanishing of the sheaf map, or the corresponding geometric-fibre map as asserted in the source, implies u(x)=0.

Section 2 introduces i:Y→X between proper smooth schemes over an algebraically closed field k and the contravariant map i* on degree 2n−1 with corrected rational coefficients Q(n). The ink direction and both degrees agree with the stated source/target; this diagnostic does not decide the closed numeral glyph by expectation.

Hypothesis a) asks for a reverse map whose restriction to im(i*) is a right inverse for i*, represented by an algebraic cycle on YxX. The star after v is present but its vertical placement is unresolved.

The author writes conjectures standart and donc est sans doute touhours vérifiée; those source spellings and the qualification sans doute are retained. The author then names a hyperplane-section case under algebraicity of Lambda and mentions lifting X with its polarization to characteristic zero. These claims were transcribed, not established in this run.

The assertion that a sheaf map vanishes if and only if its map on a displayed geometric fibre vanishes was not verified: the necessary context, including any connectedness/local-constancy hypotheses, is not supplied on this page. No extra hypotheses were inserted into the transcription.

No diagram or drawing occurs. Five displayed maps, the inline cohomology expression, all prose, handwritten page 3, archive pencil 11, seven underline rules, all identified added signs, cancellations, and the typed interline insertion are inventoried.

The initial pro in the projectifs→propres correction is live type; wholesale cancellation and handwriting of the full word would erase observed source-layer information. The final s layering remains uncertain.

H’s editorial note identifying g as the structural morphism of C is not source ink and was not incorporated. H’s bold coefficient macros and emphasis macros are treated as macro conventions where the notes acknowledge the same source reading; explicit typed-Q and typed-propres claims are separately collated.

The apparent comma or closing curve after the interline propriété is attached to a pale curved insertion leader; no independent punctuation was forced. The lower-right pale scan-edge trace was not treated as an authorial drawing.

Paragraph cues: an enlarged gap introduces section 2; a) is indented after et on suppose. The compatibility paragraph remains continuous through its displays. Ordinary wrapped lines, including the final NB, were not promoted to paragraphs.

check_events.outcome: Conditional check actually performed: assume (**) is the functorial H^1(S,−) map induced by (*) and the printed compatibility gives u(x)=H^1(S,Z)(u(x′)). If Z=0 as a sheaf homomorphism, additivity/functoriality gives H^1(S,Z)=0, so its value on u(x′) is 0. This checks only the zero-map consequence under those stated identifications; it does not verify the construction of Z or the one-fibre equivalence.

Conditional linear-map check actually performed: write A=H^(2n−1)(X,Q(n)), B=H^(2n−1)(Y,Q(n)), r=i*:A→B, and v:B→A. The printed right-inverse-on-image condition is r v|im(r)=id_im(r), equivalently r v r=r. Therefore (v r)^2=v(r v r)=v r, and (r v)^2=(r v r)v=r v. This confirms that the local wording has a consistent right-inverse meaning. It proves neither existence nor algebraicity of v and does not adjudicate the star typography.

brief_feedback: Clarify whether visible x-out characters should be encoded literally when they cancel a blank or when the old glyph cannot be separated, and how to distinguish an uncertain old-layer letter from uncertainty in the live word. The one-crop rule was sufficient; old/live source layering still requires explicit residual doubts.
